attacker_pocs.name: class_len_eq_cap
attacker_pocs.cmd: bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; so=$(find /work -name libmatio.so -printf "%T@ %p\n" | sort -n | tail -1 | cut -d" " -f2-); dir=$(dirname "$so"); pub=$(find /work -name matio_pubconf.h -printf "%T@ %p\n" | sort -n | tail -1 | cut -d" " -f2-); cc -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g $(pkg-config --cflags hdf5) -I"$(dirname "$pub")" -I/work/src -o /tmp/poc_newbug /work/pocs/newbug.c -L"$dir" -lmatio $(pkg-config --libs hdf5) -lz -lm; ASAN_OPTIONS=abort_on_error=1 LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$dir" /tmp/poc_newbug'
attacker_pocs.why: A scalar fixed-length MATLAB_class of exactly MAX_MATLAB_CLASS_LEN bytes passes the new bound (class_len > MAX is false) but H5Tset_size/H5Aread still write class_len+1 bytes into the MAX-byte buffer allocated in Mat_H5ReadVarInfo, overflowing by one byte on Mat_Open + Mat_VarReadNext.

role_a_rationale: Mat_H5ReadVarInfo now rejects a non-string, variable-length, or non-scalar MATLAB_class and refuses a datatype size above 256, so the unbounded H5Aread (non-scalar element count, VL string, or oversized class_len) returns a format error instead of overflowing. The replacement buffer is a fixed 256-byte allocation while the memory datatype is still sized class_len+1 and the terminator is stored at class_str[class_len]. A class name of length 256 is therefore accepted and H5Aread writes 257 bytes. That length is not a normal MATLAB class name, so ordinary v7.3 reads (numeric, char, struct, cell, logical) are unchanged; the parent allocator used class_len+1 and does not overflow on the same scalar attribute.
